notes.subject: language
notes.text: Mostly Cyrillic, often with Latin text beside it. The letter Ъ appears only here and in Russian, and the word for street is улица or ул.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Pole tops with 3 large alternating hook-shaped insulators, probably unique to this country; some face downward.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Most poles are round concrete with small alternating hook insulators; ladder-style concrete and plain wooden poles are less common.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Pedestrian signs show four stripes and a person wearing a hat; no other central or eastern country uses four.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Blue arrow-shaped direction signs and white town entry signs show two lines, in both scripts.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Chevrons are red on white, as in some neighbours; the southern and western ones use black and white.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Bollards are rare; they are plain, with a red reflector at the front and white at the back.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Road lines are usually thin, a handy contrast with its northern neighbour's thick lines.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Roads are often poor, with many small cracks and some potholes.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Orange tiled roofs with patches of mortar on the corner tiles, often looking uneven and badly built.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Metal trash bins of a certain shape are very common, also seen in Turkey and other Balkan countries.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Most generation 3 was shot in March and April, giving a dead-looking winter look, as also in Hungary and Czechia.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Generation 3 often shows a small piece of grey tape on the antenna tip, also seen in nearby countries.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Generation 4 cars are blue, red or black, or hidden entirely; the red car also appears in a few countries including Russia and Slovakia.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The Balkan range splits the country: flat plains to the north up to the Romanian border, another big flat area between it and the Rhodope range.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The Rhodope Mountains run southeast into Greece and hold the highest peaks.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The far west has many small valleys among hills and small mountains.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Tall pyramid-shaped peaks of two national parks are visible in the southwest.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Wind turbines are most common in the northeast province near the coast.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: White walls with brown wooden details, similar to alpine style, are common in the southern mountains.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Area codes work well for regionguessing and are ordered by first digit.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: A fully hidden generation 4 car appears along the north and west borders and the northern coast.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: The red generation 4 car is mostly in central and southeastern areas.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Generation 3 with a taped short antenna is common in the east; a taped long antenna with a white car is found in Stara Zagora.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: The old coastal towns of Nessebar and Sozopol have unpainted stone, white walls, brown wood and cobbled streets.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Bumpy-shaped mountains loom southwest of Vratsa and are visible from far away.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: The capital has white street signs with two red strips, one along the bottom and one partly across the top.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Brown street signs with bright yellow text are found in Stara Zagora.
